shortDescription: The Indonesia Stock Exchange said on Monday it has cut its lower auto-rejection limit to 7% from 15%, a move it said would support investors in making decisions.

children: The Indonesia Stock Exchange said on Monday it has cut its lower auto-rejection limit to 7% from 15%, a move it said would support investors in making decisions.
The measure is effective Monday and will run until December 31 this year

It comes after global index provider MSCI said on Friday it could downgrade Indonesia's stock market to "standalone" status, saying it was no longer worthy of emerging status, as "significant concerns remain around market dysfunction"
, the world's worst performer this year, closed down 11.57% in its biggest single-day drop in 28 years

"This adjustment is aimed at giving investors an opportunity to evaluate and digest available information, helping them make better investment decisions based on Indonesia's economic fundamentals," the exchange said in a statement
Monday's move follows a weekend meeting between the financial regulator and capital market participants, including analysts and economists
The policy will be reassessed periodically based on market conditions, the bourse said
The measure is a way for trading of particular stocks to be rejected if the price drop reaches 7%
